thread:
diego: Hey team, new hire here. On Windows 10 (home) behind a consumer router. WireGuard split-tunnel profile applied but I can't reach internal docker registry (registry.intra.redwood:5000). `docker pull` just hangs at TLS handshake. Public pulls fine. Any quick ideas?

infra-jen: welcome! First guess: home NAT/CGNAT or hairpin NAT problem between your host and the VPN gateway. Can you paste `netsh interface ipv4 show addresses` and `ipconfig /all` (redact MACs) and also try `curl -v --socks5 localhost:1080 https://registry.intra.redwood:5000/v2/` if you can ssh to bastion?

diego: netsh shows WG adapter with IP 10.30.45.9, default route still via my router 192.168.0.1. I can ssh to bastion (ssh -p2200 diego@bastion.internal) from powershell, but `curl --socks5` fails with connection refused. Docker still hanging.

sre-lin: if ssh to bastion works you can run `ssh -D 1080 -p 2200 diego@bastion.internal` then set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` env vars to `socks5h://localhost:1080` and try `docker pull` (Docker Desktop reads system proxy or use `com.docker.proxy` settings). That bypasses your home NAT for registry traffic.

diego: started `ssh -D` tunnel, set env vars, `docker pull` still hangs; `curl --socks5h` to registry returns `curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 1080: Connection refused` even though ssh -D shows active connection.

claire: two things to check: 1) Windows firewall or security suite blocking the dynamic SOCKS listener; 2) Docker Desktop's integration with WSL2 may not use Windows env vars. Try `powershell Start-Process ssh -ArgumentList '-D','1080','-N','-p','2200','diego@bastion.internal' -NoNewWindow` and then in an elevated powershell `netstat -ano | findstr 1080` to confirm listening. For WSL/Docker, run `wsl -e sh -lc 'curl --socks5h localhost:1080 https://registry.intra.redwood:5000/v2/'` to test from WSL network namespace.

diego: netstat shows LISTENING on 127.0.0.1:1080, pid matches ssh. But inside WSL curl still times out. From powershell `curl --socks5h localhost:1080 https://registry.intra.redwood:5000/v2/` returns registry API JSON quickly. So powershell -> socks -> bastion works, WSL -> socks does not.

infra-jen: known WSL quirk — localhost mapping between Windows and WSL can be flaky for proxy sockets. Workaround: in ssh -D use `-D [::1]:1080` or bind to 0.0.0.0 and restrict with firewall, then point WSL to Windows host IP instead of localhost. Example: `ssh -D 0.0.0.0:1080 -N -p 2200 diego@bastion.internal` then in WSL `export ALL_PROXY=socks5h://$(cat /etc/resolv.conf | grep nameserver | awk '{print $2}'):1080` (Windows host IP appear there). Be careful opening 0.0.0.0; prefer loopback workaround if possible.

sre-lin: another option: enable Docker Desktop's "Use the same proxy as Windows" toggle or configure Docker daemon.json to use the registry proxy. For a quick unblock, you can `docker pull` on Windows and then use images in WSL by saving/loading.

diego: bound to 0.0.0.0 and pointed WSL at host IP, `curl` inside WSL now gets registry API and `docker pull` in WSL started. Thanks!

deploy-bot: INF-1200 created: "windows home NAT + wsl socks mapping - onboarding doc" assigned to eng-infra.

diego: I'll add a short note to the onboarding checklist about SSH SOCKS binding and WSL testing. Appreciate the help! :raised_hands:
